title: TerminologyAnalysis
topic: Direct empirical methods for cross-version multimodal document element lineage and hierarchical provenance, with special attention to revised workbook provenance and message referring-expression grounding into versioned pages, regions, and cells.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Broad umbrella for machine learning and computer-vision methods that extract, classify, parse, reason over, or answer questions about documents using text, layout, and visual information.
seed_audit.main_risk: It is far broader than version lineage, provenance, or grounded reference resolution and is often used as a field or product label rather than a sharply defined task.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: OCR, document classification, key-value extraction, form understanding, generic document foundation models, and commercial document-processing systems with no version or evidence-location semantics.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Umbrella term overlapping document AI, information extraction, OCR, layout analysis, document classification, and document question answering; also common in commercial product terminology.
seed_audit.main_risk: Low terminological precision and strong contamination by vendor literature.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Commercial intelligent document processing, invoice extraction, workflow automation, OCR services, and generic enterprise document processing.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Joint modeling of document text, two-dimensional layout, and visual appearance for tasks such as classification, extraction, and question answering.
seed_audit.main_risk: Most work is single-version and does not preserve element identity or provenance across revisions.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Single-page forms, receipts, invoices, classification benchmarks, and key-value extraction without revision alignment or exact evidence lineage.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Abbreviation commonly used for visually rich document understanding, especially multimodal models combining textual, layout, and image information.
seed_audit.main_risk: The acronym is less stable than the expanded phrase and can be ambiguous outside document-understanding literature.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Generic multimodal document models and unrelated uses of the acronym.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Detection, segmentation, classification, ordering, and geometric organization of document regions such as text blocks, tables, figures, headers, and columns.
seed_audit.main_risk: Layout segmentation alone provides coordinates but not semantic correspondence across versions or answer provenance.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Page segmentation, region detection, reading-order reconstruction, and layout classification evaluated independently of semantic grounding or version lineage.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Language or multimodal models that incorporate two-dimensional coordinates, visual features, or document structure alongside text.
seed_audit.main_risk: A model can be layout-aware without producing stable source identities, exact evidence localization, or cross-version correspondences.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Document classification, form extraction, receipt extraction, and single-page token labeling.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Extraction of entities, fields, relations, key-value pairs, tables, or structured records from documents.
seed_audit.main_risk: Extraction targets are normally values or entities rather than persistent evidence objects with cross-version lineage.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Named-entity recognition, invoice field extraction, receipt parsing, form understanding, and relation extraction with no exact source hierarchy.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Question answering over document images using textual, visual, and layout evidence.
seed_audit.main_risk: Many benchmarks score answer text only; answer correctness does not imply correct page, region, cell, or version provenance.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Document QA systems returning strings without evidence localization, single-page QA, and models using OCR tokens without explicit grounding.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Established task and benchmark family for visual question answering over document images.
seed_audit.main_risk: The label covers several subtasks and does not by itself imply multi-page evidence localization, version awareness, or cell-level provenance.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Answer-only DocVQA systems, OCR benchmarks presented through DocVQA, and single-page benchmark improvements.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Methods that jointly process, retrieve, route, or reason over multiple pages of one document.
seed_audit.main_risk: Page selection and multi-page reasoning can still omit exact region lineage and document-revision identity.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Page retrieval, page classification, document summarization, and long-context QA without spatial evidence.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Multimodal reasoning over documents whose text, pages, tables, figures, and visual structure exceed ordinary single-page or short-context assumptions.
seed_audit.main_risk: The term is recent and broad, and often emphasizes context length rather than provenance.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Long-context multimodal language models, video-like page sequence models, document summarization, and benchmark scaling studies without grounded evidence.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Informal compound term for combining OCR output with geometric or structural document analysis.
seed_audit.main_risk: It is not a stable academic task name and may collapse two distinct problems: recognition and structural interpretation.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: OCR accuracy, text detection, word recognition, bounding-box prediction, and OCR post-processing.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Prediction of the logical sequence in which document regions, lines, or blocks should be read.
seed_audit.main_risk: It protects structural interpretation but does not address version lineage or referring-expression grounding.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Page segmentation and reading-order benchmarks with no semantic QA, provenance, or revision component.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Localization of table regions within document pages or images.
seed_audit.main_risk: Bounding a table does not reconstruct its cells, headers, merged relationships, formulas, or provenance.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Object detection for table bounding boxes and document-layout benchmarks.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Recovery of table rows, columns, cells, spanning cells, and structural topology from page images or document representations.
seed_audit.main_risk: TSR normally reconstructs visible table geometry only and does not cover workbook formulas, hidden structures, cross-sheet references, or revision lineage.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Image-table extraction benchmarks where tables are isolated snapshots and no semantic or version information exists.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Broad family covering table structure, header interpretation, semantic typing, relation understanding, table representation learning, and reasoning over tabular data.
seed_audit.main_risk: The term spans both document-image tables and relational tables and can lose spreadsheet-specific semantics.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Web tables, database tables, knowledge-table matching, and table representation learning with no document or workbook provenance.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Answering natural-language questions using structured or semi-structured tables, often by selecting cells, executing operations, or generating answers.
seed_audit.main_risk: Most Table QA assumes an already-correct table and does not test extraction completeness, workbook versioning, or exact visual provenance.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Semantic parsing over clean relational tables, synthetic table reasoning, and answer-only QA.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Broad study of spreadsheet structure, formulas, cell roles, layout, table regions, semantics, dependencies, reasoning, and increasingly language-model interaction with workbooks.
seed_audit.main_risk: The phrase is broad and newer papers may call narrow formula prediction or table reconstruction comprehensive spreadsheet understanding.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Single-sheet table QA, CSV reasoning, formula completion alone, spreadsheet generation, and benchmark tasks that discard hidden sheets, formatting, names, or revision history.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Recognition and reasoning over graphical charts, including axes, legends, marks, values, relationships, and underlying data.
seed_audit.main_risk: Charts are only one embedded object class and chart understanding rarely addresses attachment revisions or message-to-region references.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Chart classification, chart-to-table conversion, visual summarization, and chart captioning.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Question answering over chart images using visual, textual, and numeric reasoning.
seed_audit.main_risk: Useful for embedded-chart semantics but peripheral to the unresolved version, workbook, and reference-grounding gaps.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Synthetic chart reasoning and benchmark QA without source-location or attachment provenance.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Extraction of entities and relations using more than one modality, such as text plus document layout, images, or visual features.
seed_audit.main_risk: The term also covers social media, video, web pages, and image-text posts unrelated to document evidence.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Social-media multimodal NER, image-text relation extraction, video information extraction, and generic vision-language extraction.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Resolving expressions to entities when antecedents or referents may be distributed across linguistic and visual modalities.
seed_audit.main_risk: Most empirical work is grounded in dialogue, images, video, or embodied environments rather than office documents and attachment versions.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Visual-dialogue coreference, video coreference, embodied-agent reference resolution, and social-media entity coreference.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Resolving a referring expression in one modality to an entity or region represented in another modality; terminology overlaps multimodal coreference and referring-expression grounding.
seed_audit.main_risk: The phrase is less standardized than referring-expression grounding or multimodal coreference.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Cross-modal retrieval, image-text matching, entity linking, and multimodal alignment without an explicit referring expression.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Associating linguistic descriptions, phrases, or tokens with visual objects, regions, or coordinates.
seed_audit.main_risk: Generic visual grounding is dominated by natural-image object localization and usually lacks document hierarchy, versions, cells, and discourse context.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Natural-image phrase grounding, open-vocabulary detection, image-text alignment, autonomous-driving grounding, and robotics.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Identification or localization of the visual entity denoted by a referring expression, commonly evaluated on natural-image datasets.
seed_audit.main_risk: Standard formulations assume one image and visible objects rather than versioned documents, tables, or attachments.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: RefCOCO-style natural-image object localization and referring-expression generation.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Grounding a question, phrase, claim, or answer to a spatial region or set of regions in a document image or page.
seed_audit.main_risk: The phrase is useful but not fully standardized; relevant papers may instead use evidence localization, spatial grounding, answer grounding, or region-level attribution.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Layout detection without language grounding and visual grounding on non-document images.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Localization of evidence or cited material associated with a claim or generated answer; depending on the field it may mean identifying a cited paper, passage, sentence, or source span rather than a visual document region.
seed_audit.main_risk: The term is overloaded between scholarly citation analysis, retrieval-augmented generation attribution, and precise document evidence localization.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Citation recommendation, bibliometrics, citation-function classification, citation-context detection, and RAG citation generation without spatial grounding.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Recognition and structural or semantic interpretation of document pages available primarily as raster images.
seed_audit.main_risk: The term often reduces to OCR and layout extraction rather than evidence lineage.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: OCR, historical-document transcription, document restoration, binarization, and image enhancement.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Comparison of two or more revisions to identify additions, deletions, moves, formatting changes, structural differences, or semantic changes.
seed_audit.main_risk: The phrase is not a single standardized academic task and can retrieve software tools, textual diff, legal redlining, or near-duplicate detection rather than persistent element lineage.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Text diff utilities, plagiarism detection, near-duplicate detection, legal redlining products, version-control tutorials, and document similarity.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Detection of visual changes between document renderings or page images, often using image registration, change detection, or layout comparison.
seed_audit.main_risk: Pixel or geometric differences do not establish semantic correspondence or whether a region is the same logical element after revision.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Image differencing, screenshot regression testing, webpage visual testing, and pixel-level change detection.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Operational phrase for extracting text or structured content from attached files; not a stable academic task name.
seed_audit.main_risk: Searches are likely to return software documentation, security tooling, email parsers, and ETL products rather than empirical document-understanding research.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Email parser libraries, malware analysis, attachment download systems, enterprise ETL, and API documentation.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Product-oriented description of reasoning over files attached to email; it is not an established academic task label.
seed_audit.main_risk: Low recall for the relevant academic literature and high contamination by cybersecurity, email forensics, and product documentation.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Malware attachment analysis, spam/phishing detection, MIME processing, email forensics, and commercial attachment extraction.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Broad interpretation of rasterized user interfaces or screen images, including OCR, UI element detection, screen question answering, and agent grounding.
seed_audit.main_risk: The dominant literature concerns user interfaces and autonomous agents rather than screenshots embedded in workplace messages or documents.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: GUI agents, screen navigation, mobile UI parsing, web agents, accessibility, and screenshot captioning.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Alignment between a figure, subfigure, visual region, or figure element and text describing it, often in scientific documents.
seed_audit.main_risk: It usually links captions or prose to figures rather than arbitrary message references to highlighted regions or revised attachments.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Figure-caption matching, scientific figure retrieval, caption generation, and subfigure segmentation without discourse reference resolution.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Retrieval or ranking of documents, pages, or document elements using text, images, layout, or multiple modalities.
seed_audit.main_risk: Retrieval identifies candidates but does not prove exact evidence grounding, version lineage, or semantic correspondence.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Cross-modal retrieval, page retrieval, enterprise search, document embedding, and image-text retrieval without provenance.

task_families.name: Cross-version document alignment and element correspondence
task_families.description: Align successive revisions of a document and determine which page, region, block, table, figure, or other element in one version corresponds to which element in another, including moves, splits, merges, insertions, deletions, and changed content.
task_families.why_it_matters: This is the central missing mechanism for carrying an older citation or grounded region forward to its later counterpart instead of treating each attachment version as an unrelated document.
seed_papers: XyDiff: An Algorithm and Tool for the Detection of Changes in XML Documents

task_families.name: Document evolution, semantic differencing, and persistent element identity
task_families.description: Represent document revisions as an evolution history in which document components retain or acquire persistent identities and changes are classified structurally or semantically rather than only as text edits.
task_families.why_it_matters: Stable attachment identity and persistent element identity are prerequisites for version-relative provenance and semantic change tracking.
seed_papers: XyDiff: An Algorithm and Tool for the Detection of Changes in XML Documents

task_families.name: Spreadsheet and workbook structural-semantic understanding
task_families.description: Model spreadsheets as workbooks containing sheets, regions, headers, formulas, formatting, merged cells, hidden structures, named ranges, units, cross-sheet references, and other semantics beyond a flat table.
task_families.why_it_matters: The target system must preserve workbook meaning that is invisible if an XLSX file is reduced to displayed cell values or CSV.
seed_papers: TUTA: Tree-based Transformers for Generally Structured Table Pre-training

task_families.name: Spreadsheet formula dependency, auditing, and cell-level provenance
task_families.description: Recover, analyze, or trace formula dependencies and cell-to-cell relationships, including cross-sheet dependency graphs and explanations of how derived values depend on source cells.
task_families.why_it_matters: Formula dependency and cell lineage are natural primitives for provenance inside one workbook state and can support later cross-version cell lineage.

task_families.name: Versioned spreadsheet and workbook lineage
task_families.description: Relate cells, ranges, formulas, sheets, names, and structural regions across workbook revisions and identify semantic changes while preserving their history.
task_families.why_it_matters: This directly targets the unresolved requirement that a cell or range cited in an older workbook remain traceable after rows, columns, sheets, formulas, or names change.

task_families.name: Message-to-document referring-expression grounding
task_families.description: Resolve discourse expressions such as this screenshot, the highlighted row, numbers below, that table, or attachment v2 to a concrete attachment object, version, page, region, table, cell, or range.
task_families.why_it_matters: This is the exact handoff from textual reference resolution into Topic 08 and is currently unvalidated for workplace-style communication.

task_families.name: Document-region and cell-level evidence grounding
task_families.description: Ground a question, generated answer, claim, or extracted fact to exact document evidence such as a page, bounding region, table cell, or source span.
task_families.why_it_matters: It supplies the fine-grained evidence anchors needed below attachment and page level.
seed_papers: DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images
MP-DocVQA: Benchmarking Multi-Page Document Visual Question Answering

task_families.name: Multi-page document visual question answering and evidence routing
task_families.description: Answer questions over multi-page documents while selecting relevant pages and, where supported, localizing evidence within them.
task_families.why_it_matters: It tests document hierarchy above region level and provides evidence about page routing, long-document scaling, and the gap between answer correctness and evidence localization.
seed_papers: MP-DocVQA: Benchmarking Multi-Page Document Visual Question Answering
DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images

task_families.name: Visually rich document representation and layout-aware extraction
task_families.description: Encode text, two-dimensional layout, and visual features so document regions, tables, and other elements retain structural context during extraction and reasoning.
task_families.why_it_matters: This provides the representation layer needed before fine-grained provenance can be trusted, although it is insufficient by itself.
seed_papers: LayoutLM: Pre-training of Text and Layout for Document Image Understanding
LayoutLMv2: Multi-modal Pre-training for Visually-rich Document Understanding
LayoutLMv3: Pre-training for Document AI with Unified Text and Image Masking
Donut: Document Understanding Transformer without OCR

task_families.name: Table structure recognition and semantic table understanding
task_families.description: Recover table cells, spanning structure, hierarchical headers, row-column associations, and semantic relationships required before cell-level grounding or QA.
task_families.why_it_matters: Incorrect structural reconstruction can produce apparently valid cell values attached to the wrong row, column, header, unit, or merged region.
seed_papers: PubTables-1M: Towards Comprehensive Table Extraction From Unstructured Documents
TAPAS: Weakly Supervised Table Parsing via Pre-training

task_families.name: Fine-grained data provenance and lineage
task_families.description: Database and data-management work formalizing where results came from, which source items contributed to them, and how provenance propagates through transformations.
task_families.why_it_matters: Where-provenance, why-provenance, lineage, and provenance propagation provide formal vocabulary and representation ideas for the requested source hierarchy, even though ordinary databases do not contain document pages and visual regions.
seed_papers: Why and Where: A Characterization of Data Provenance

task_families.name: Visual referring-expression comprehension and phrase grounding
task_families.description: Resolve linguistic descriptions to visual objects or regions, usually in natural images.
task_families.why_it_matters: It provides mature grounding objectives and evaluation methods that may transfer to references such as the highlighted row or red box, but it lacks document-version and workplace discourse structure.
seed_papers: MDETR: Modulated Detection for End-to-End Multi-Modal Understanding

task_families.name: Multimodal coreference and grounded reference resolution
task_families.description: Resolve linguistic expressions across turns or discourse when the referent is represented visually or in another modality.
task_families.why_it_matters: Unlike ordinary phrase grounding, this family can model discourse history, deixis, and repeated references, which are important for message-to-attachment grounding.

task_families.name: Scientific-document evidence localization and source-span attribution
task_families.description: Question answering or claim support over scientific documents where systems identify supporting passages, evidence spans, pages, or document sections in addition to producing an answer.
task_families.why_it_matters: It provides evidence-supervision and attribution patterns relevant to the page/element/span layers of hierarchical provenance, while usually lacking workplace attachments and spreadsheet cells.
seed_papers: QASPER: A Dataset for Question Answering over Scientific Research Papers

task_families.name: Document image registration, visual change detection, and page correspondence
task_families.description: Geometrically align page images or layouts and detect changed regions across scans, renderings, or document versions.
task_families.why_it_matters: Geometric correspondence can bootstrap cross-version region alignment when revisions preserve substantial visual structure, but it cannot by itself establish semantic identity.

task_families.name: Failure-aware document QA and extraction evaluation
task_families.description: Evaluate answerability, abstention, OCR and parser failures, localization errors, structural corruption, and extraction completeness rather than scoring only successful answers.
task_families.why_it_matters: The product must distinguish genuine evidence absence from failures in parsing, OCR, table reconstruction, retrieval, grounding, or unsupported content.

task_families.name: Long-document and large-workbook robustness and scaling
task_families.description: Measure quality, latency, memory, routing, and failure behavior as page counts, table sizes, workbook sizes, and structural complexity increase.
task_families.why_it_matters: The open engineering gaps require workload-realistic evidence rather than only accuracy on small single-page examples.
seed_papers: MP-DocVQA: Benchmarking Multi-Page Document Visual Question Answering

task_families.name: Screenshot, GUI, and visual-region grounding
task_families.description: Ground instructions or referring expressions to regions and interface elements in screenshots or rendered screens.
task_families.why_it_matters: This is a closer visual analogue than natural-image grounding for references to screenshots embedded in workplace communication, while still differing from static attachments and revision lineage.

downgrade_rules: Downgrade papers that detect or OCR text but do not preserve document structure, source coordinates, or evidence identity.
Downgrade papers that report answer accuracy without evidence localization when the claimed contribution is provenance or grounding.
Downgrade single-version document methods when they are used as evidence for cross-version lineage; they may support representation or extraction only.
Downgrade textual diff methods that cannot align moved, split, merged, reformatted, rasterized, or structurally transformed document elements.
Downgrade visual diff or image-change methods that detect pixel differences without semantic element correspondence.
Downgrade near-duplicate detection, plagiarism detection, and document-similarity work unless it establishes revision identity or element-level correspondence.
Downgrade generic version control or source-code differencing unless the method is empirically evaluated on document, XML, spreadsheet, or comparable structured artifacts.
Downgrade XML-tree differencing as TRANSFER evidence when the target evidence is rendered PDF, image regions, or spreadsheet semantics not represented in the XML task.
Downgrade document layout analysis that stops at bounding boxes or region classes without linking those regions to language, evidence, or revisions.
Downgrade table detection when cells, row-column topology, spanning cells, hierarchical headers, units, or reading order are not reconstructed.
Downgrade table QA conducted on clean pre-extracted tables when making claims about PDF table extraction or workbook preservation.
Downgrade spreadsheet work that converts sheets to CSV or flat tables and therefore discards formulas, formatting, merged cells, hidden structures, names, or cross-sheet references.
Downgrade formula prediction or formula repair when it does not expose dependency or provenance relationships relevant to source tracing.
Downgrade workbook reasoning evaluated on a single sheet when it is used to support claims about cross-sheet references, workbook-level semantics, or hidden sheets.
Downgrade within-state spreadsheet provenance when it is used as evidence for provenance across workbook revisions.
Downgrade natural-image referring-expression comprehension to TRANSFER unless the study uses documents, tables, screenshots, interfaces, or another structurally comparable surface.
Downgrade image-text retrieval and contrastive alignment when there is no explicit referring expression and no localized referent.
Downgrade visual dialogue coreference to TRANSFER unless referents are document elements or structurally comparable screen objects.
Downgrade screenshot or GUI grounding to TRANSFER when the screenshot is an interactive interface rather than evidence embedded in a workplace attachment.
Downgrade citation recommendation, bibliometrics, or citation-function classification; these do not provide source-location provenance.
Downgrade RAG citation-generation papers when a citation identifies only a document or passage and does not validate the required page, region, cell, or answer-span hierarchy.
Downgrade retrieval papers that find the correct attachment or page but do not ground the final answer to precise evidence.
Downgrade multi-page QA that selects the correct page but provides no region or span localization when used to support fine-grained provenance.
Downgrade scientific-PDF evidence localization to TRANSFER when it lacks attachment version identity or cross-version element lineage.
Downgrade OCR-free document models if their evaluation cannot distinguish omitted content from correctly absent content.
Downgrade parser benchmarks that report throughput or syntax coverage without measuring whether tables, images, layout, reading order, or unsupported features were preserved.
Downgrade robustness studies that perturb OCR text only if they do not test structural corruption, merged tables, irregular reading order, embedded visuals, or scanned pages.
Downgrade benchmark results that exclude unsupported examples from denominators; extraction completeness and failure accounting must remain explicit.
Downgrade systems that silently return an empty result when extraction or grounding is unsupported; this violates the product distinction between genuine absence and processing failure.
Downgrade provenance representations that identify only a source document but cannot represent at least one finer-grained level such as page, region, element, cell, or span.

Downgrade a paper from DIRECT to TRANSFER if its empirical domain removes the central difficulty being claimed, such as using a clean relational table instead of a workbook or a single static image instead of a revision sequence.

Do not treat combining several papers that separately solve document identity, page localization, region grounding, and cell provenance as validation of one end-to-end hierarchical provenance representation.
Do not treat a filename, URL, or attachment label as stable document identity unless the method explicitly validates identity across renaming, replacement, or revision.
Do not treat lexical similarity between old and new regions as lineage unless correspondence is empirically validated against moves, edits, splits, merges, or structural changes.
Do not treat synthetic or transfer-domain success as evidence of production-email accuracy; retain the DIRECT versus TRANSFER distinction.

date_policy.rationale: Discovery must reach at least 1990. The target combines several literatures whose modern neural forms are recent but whose foundations are substantially older: document image analysis, page segmentation, reading order, table recognition, document matching, and image registration were established before modern Document AI; database provenance and XML change tracking became important in the early 2000s; modern DocVQA, layout-aware transformers, and multimodal foundation models are mostly much later. A 2018, 2020, or similarly recent cutoff would therefore silently remove foundations needed to interpret persistent identity, structural correspondence, provenance, and document-layout evaluation. Round 4 should still prioritize recent direct evidence, but discovery should permit foundational results from 1990 onward.
